name: Nmap
what: A free network scanner for host discovery, port scanning, service and OS fingerprinting, plus the Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE) for vulnerability and misconfiguration checks. It is the default first tool on almost every authorized network assessment.
when: To map which ports and services are really open on hosts you are responsible for, to confirm a firewall change, and to run carefully chosen NSE scripts against an approved scope before heavier scanners.
cost_note: Free for end users under the NPSL; embedding Nmap in commercial products needs an OEM license.
example: Get written approval and the exact list of IP ranges in scope; tell the SOC the source IP and window.
Service and version scan live hosts with controlled timing: `nmap -sS -sV -p 1-1024 --top-ports 1000 -T3 -oA svc-2026-10 10.0.10.0/24`.
For a single agreed host, add safe default scripts: `nmap -sV -sC -p 22,80,443,445 target.contoso.lab -oA host-check`.
Diff open ports against the CMDB and firewall policy; ticket every unexpected listener.
pitfalls: Aggressive timing (`-T4`/`-T5`) and intrusive NSE scripts can disrupt printers, OT and old appliances; escalate timing only after a gentle pass.
Scanning networks you do not own or have permission for can be illegal.
Version detection and scripts generate more traffic and louder logs; keep them inside the signed window.
